skill.name: streaming-llm-responses
skill.description: Implement real-time streaming UI patterns for AI chat applications using ChatKit lifecycle handlers, progress updates, client effects, and client tools.
skill.summary: Build responsive AI chat interfaces with streaming status, progress events, and synchronized client state.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, and a manual verification command. The network finding is also a false positive because the referenced line uses a placeholder function, not an HTTP client. The remaining issues are semantic guidance gaps around client-state minimization and validation of server-sent UI effect payloads.

remediation.issue: Client tools can expose broad client-side state.
remediation.suggestion: Document strict allowlists for each client tool, redact sensitive form fields, and return only fields needed for the current user action.

remediation.issue: Client effects mutate UI from server-provided payloads.
remediation.suggestion: Add schema validation examples for effect names and payloads, and ignore unknown or malformed effects before mutating UI state.

semantic_findings.title: Client Tool Data Minimization Gap
semantic_findings.description: The examples show client tools returning selected item IDs, viewport coordinates, and form values to the AI. Without guidance to whitelist fields or redact sensitive values, implementations may expose private client-side state beyond what a request needs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples directly return client-side state and form values. The risk depends on application data sensitivity, so this is a real privacy concern rather than confirmed malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Client Effect Payloads
semantic_findings.description: The examples apply server-sent effect data directly to status, map, selection, and notification handlers. They do not show payload validation before state mutation, which can cause incorrect or unauthorized UI changes in production implementations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples clearly mutate UI state from effect payloads without validation. The finding is lower confidence because sample code often omits production validation for brevity.

content.value_statement: Real-time AI chat feels broken when users cannot see progress, response state, or UI changes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code patterns for streaming lifecycles, progress events, client effects, and client tools.
actual_capabilities: Explains useChatKit response lifecycle handlers for start, end, error, and thread loading states.
Shows how to emit and handle ClientEffectEvent updates for status, notifications, map movement, and selections.
Provides ProgressUpdateEvent patterns for long-running backend work.
Documents client tool handlers for selected items, viewport data, and form state.
Includes a reference page with a full streaming ChatKit configuration.
limitations: It provides implementation patterns, not a runnable application.
Examples use placeholder API URLs, domain keys, stores, maps, and form refs.
It does not define authentication, authorization, or data retention policies.
Client tool examples need project-specific validation and redaction before production use.

use_cases.title: Add response lifecycle feedback
use_cases.description: Implement locked interaction states, loading overlays, and error recovery around streaming AI responses.

use_cases.title: Stream progress during long work
use_cases.description: Show clear progress messages while backend tools search, analyze, or process user requests.

use_cases.title: Synchronize assistant actions with UI state
use_cases.description: Connect AI events to maps, forms, canvases, or simulations through client effects and client tools.

prompt_templates.title: Add basic streaming state
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new ChatKit interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the streaming-llm-responses skill to add response start, response end, and error handlers to my ChatKit component. Keep the UI locked only while the assistant is responding.

prompt_templates.title: Show backend progress
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate backend work with visible status updates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design progress updates for a long-running assistant tool. Include user-facing status messages for search, processing, and finalization.

prompt_templates.title: Handle client effects
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced UI updates driven by assistant events.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to wire client effects for status updates, notifications, and map movement. Include validation rules for every effect payload before changing UI state.

prompt_templates.title: Design client tool contracts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced state query design for production systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define client tools that return only approved state to the assistant. Include field allowlists, redaction rules, and error behavior for unknown tools.

output_examples.input: A React chat panel lets users click map objects while the assistant is still responding.
output_examples.output: The result explains how to lock map interaction at response start, unlock it at response end, and always unlock after errors.

output_examples.input: A backend assistant searches many articles before answering.
output_examples.output: The result describes progress messages for search, counting results, processing batches, and finalizing the response.

output_examples.input: An assistant needs current form values before recommending the next step.
output_examples.output: The result outlines a client tool contract that returns approved fields only and rejects unknown tool requests.

best_practices: Lock interactive UI during responses and always unlock it on errors.
Validate each client effect name and payload before updating application state.
Return the smallest safe client tool result and redact sensitive fields.
anti_patterns: Treating server-sent effect data as trusted UI commands.
Returning complete form state to the model when only one field is needed.
Leaving users without progress messages during slow backend work.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps developers build responsive AI chat interfaces that show streaming progress and keep UI state synchronized.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that developers adapt to an existing ChatKit application.

faq.question: Can it help with client tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how client tools can return selected items, viewport information, and form data to the assistant.

faq.question: What should teams review before production use?
faq.answer: Teams should validate effect payloads and limit client tool responses to approved, non-sensitive fields.

faq.question: Does the skill make network requests by itself?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The network-like line in the reference is a placeholder processing function inside an example.
